message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several statutory rights designed to protect them from unfair treatment and ensure safe, habitable living conditions. Here’s a quick overview: | Area | Key Rights (Texas Property Code) | |------|----------------------------------| | **Security Deposits** | • Landlords may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit and two months for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after the lease ends, minus any lawful deductions. | | **Habitability** | • Landlords must keep the premises in good repair, maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, and structural integrity.
• Must provide working smoke detectors and secure windows/doors. | | **Rent Increases** | • No limit on how much a landlord can raise rent, but it must be in writing and given at least 30 days’ notice for month‑to‑month leases. | | **Lease Terms** | • Written lease required for month‑to‑month agreements.
• Landlord must provide a copy of the lease and any amendments. | | **Entry Notice** | • Landlord must give at least 24 hours written notice before entering, except in emergencies. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | | **Repair & Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to fix major problems, tenants may pay for repairs and deduct the cost from rent, but only after giving written notice and waiting 30 days. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must serve a written notice (usually 3 days for nonpayment, 30 days for lease termination).
• Eviction must go through court; landlords cannot forcibly remove tenants. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Tenants have the right to live without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | | **Subletting & Assignment** | • Tenants may sublet or assign the lease with landlord’s written consent, which cannot be unreasonably withheld. | | **Fair Housing** | • Landlords must comply with federal Fair Housing Act and Texas Fair Housing Act. | ### Practical Tips 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of all communications, receipts, and photos of any maintenance issues. 2. **Written Notices** – Always send notices via certified mail or email with read receipt to establish proof. 3. **Know Your Lease** – Read your lease carefully; it may contain additional obligations or restrictions beyond the law. 4. **Seek Legal Aid** – If you face eviction or disputes, consider contacting a local tenant‑rights organization or legal aid clinic. If you need a more detailed explanation or help drafting a lease or notice, let me know!
